Home / Rent & Statements

Rent collection you can follow, line by line

Rent comes in, invoices go out, and you receive the balance with a statement that shows what happened.

The PayProp model

Four steps from tenant to landlord

1. Tenant pays rent

Rent is paid into the PayProp-linked RBS account.

2. Work becomes an invoice

Every piece of work done on a property is entered into PayProp as an invoice.

3. Deductions happen automatically

When rent arrives, PayProp deducts contractor invoices and expenses.

4. You receive the balance

PayProp sends the remaining balance to the landlord.

Sample statement

How to read a landlord rent statement

This example shows the shape of a statement: money in, each deduction, and what is paid out. It is deliberately simple.

  • Rent received is the starting point.
  • Each deduction names what it was for.
  • The landlord payout is the rent left after every deduction.

An audit trail by design

Because every piece of work is entered as an invoice before it is deducted, each deduction has an invoice behind it.

Payments, protection and redress

The practical details of how money moves, and what protects it, are set out in your written agreement.

Payment timing

Payment dates are set out in your management agreement and shown on every statement.

If there are insufficient funds

If rent has not arrived, or does not cover an invoice, the shortfall is shown on your statement, carried forward and explained to you.

Client money protection

The client money protection arrangements that apply to your agreement are set out in your written terms of business.

Redress scheme

Details of the redress scheme that applies to your agreement are set out in your written terms of business.

This website does not process payments or hold money, and there is no landlord login or online financial dashboard. Statements are described here for illustration.
